title: Consolidation gateway: triage and prioritization rubric for enterprise SDK language/auth/streaming requests
creator: Lydia Park
description:
Problem: Over the last 6 months we've seen a steady stream of enterprise requests for SDKs and client libraries. Requests cluster into three high-friction areas: language support gaps (Java/.NET/Go versus our dominant Python/Node), authentication patterns (SAML/SSO, OAuth token exchange, long-lived API keys), and streaming ergonomics (cursor-based partial responses, reconnect/resume behavior, backpressure APIs).

Goal: Create a single intake + prioritization gateway and a reproducible rubric that lets PM/Eng/Design quickly classify, score, and route SDK requests for enterprise customers, and surface actionable engineering work that aligns with Dedicated/Private deployment constraints and security requirements.

What this ticket is: discovery + spec for the gateway and rubric, including: scoring matrix, mandatory fields for intake (customer size, compliance need, integration type), mapped engineering owners, and an initial backlog of SDK adapter work items (language ports, auth patterns, streaming helper primitives).

Customer signals: Recent inbound notes from FinanceCorp (SAML + strict session rotation), MedServe (on-prem with strict KMS integration), and AdPlatform (Java + streaming low-latency) — consolidated in the attached intake spreadsheet.

Links and artifacts:
- Draft PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/PM-27501+SDK+Consolidation+Gateway
- Intake spreadsheet (customer rows & scoring examples): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-sdk-intake
- Proposed SDK adapter spec (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-adapters/pull/42
- Notes from partner call (MedServe): https://drive.google.com/open?id=notes-medserve-2026-02-18

Key constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: building full Java/.NET SDKs in this ticket. We are defining the prioritization and adapter spec and landing a small reference implementation for Java streaming helpers.
- Constraint: Any recommended solution must be compatible with Redwood Private (no hosted-only auth flows) and must pass a security review for enterprise SSO flows.

Hypothesis: A small set of primitives (language adapters + auth composables + streaming helper library) will cover >=80% of enterprise requests and reduce bespoke engineering work by ~60% for each new customer.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring rubric defined and documented with example scored requests from 6 customers
Intake form template created (Confluence + Google Form) and linked to sales/solutions engineers
Prioritized backlog (top 6 SDK adapter tasks) created and assigned to engineering owners
Reference Java streaming helper prototype merged in repo and demoed to internal SDK reviewers
Security checklist for SSO/OAuth paths agreed with security and added to intake fields
decision_notes:
2026-03-05: Decided to prioritize a "scoring matrix that weighs customer compliance and deployment mode (Private/Dedicated) higher than raw developer count." Engineering effort estimates will be captured as T-shirt sizes (S/M/L) in the backlog and re-scored during grooming.

Trade-offs discussed: building full idiomatic SDKs for Java/.NET is costly and low velocity; instead we will create a language adapter pattern and a canonical reference implementation for streaming and auth that can be forked.

Security review: Omar confirmed SSO flows will require a formal security review; we will gate any SAML/OAuth work behind the security checklist (attached).
